mechanic: A lying link in a chain: one witness's word reaches the narrator by two carriers, and one of them changed it.
note: Spoilers. The logic written before the prose, in the shape sketched in docs/archipelago-plan.md (questions[].needs lists alternative sets of clues; here each question has one set). `frame` is what the narrator's own prose always carries; `clues` are the units that could be case files. `facts` names the world model's facts that realise a clue; `false_trail` marks a clue put in on purpose to tempt a wrong answer.

frame.says: The bonded store on the quay was broken open on Tuesday night about ten; the town names Tobias Wren.
Marta Quill keeps the harbour lamp and looks straight down on the quay. She has no voice and writes whatever she has to say; the narrator knows her hand.

questions.asks: Where did Marta see Wren at ten o'clock?

rules_out.the chapel: c.paper: her own hand says the quay

rules_out.Pike: the changed word is the chapel, which only Elsie carried; c.pike_report agrees with c.paper
rules_out.Marta herself: c.paper: what she wrote for Elsie said the quay

clues.source: Pike, the harbourmaster, who read it on Marta's slate at first light on Wednesday
clues.says: Marta saw Wren on the quay, under her lamp, at ten.

clues.source: Elsie Quill, Marta's niece, sent down with her aunt's word on Wednesday at noon
clues.says: Marta saw Wren at the chapel door at ten.

clues.source: A folded paper in Marta's hand, with Elsie's name on the outside
clues.says: Take this to the constable. At ten Wren was on the quay, under my lamp.
The paper lay in the basket Elsie left at the narrator's door.
clues.note: Where the paper was found is itself evidence (it reached Elsie). A case file is meant to be complete without its find-spot: see docs/authored-stories.md, What the miniatures showed.

clues.says: Pike and Wren came to blows in the spring; Elsie and Wren are to be married.
clues.false_trail: A reason for each carrier to lie, so that motive decides nothing.
